Comme le veut la tradition, malgré quelques entorses à Dijon ou à Annecy, les Verts se déplaceront à Clermont un samedi.

La Ligue a en effet détaillé le programme de la 1ère journée des matchs retour : l'ASSE se déplacera samedi 23 janvier à 20h chez l'actuel 16ème du championnat.

Pour rappel, les Verts s'étaient imposés 3-1 au match aller grâce à Cardona, Ballo et Breum.

La saison dernière c'est Boakye et Stassin qui avaient permis aux Verts de s'imposer (2-1) en Auvergne.

#222224. Access, Not Chances: How Como Took Manchester United Apart – LC

Access, Not Chances: How Como Took Manchester United Apart – LC

📅 24 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4249 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • von Next Generation am 24.10.2026 in den Kategorien Champions League,Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.
  • It has been revealed that como beat Manchester United 4-1 — and in this case the scoreline really is a fair expression of the game.
  • Recent findings suggest that cesc Fàbregas’s side indicated two things that rarely go together.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

von Next Generation am 24.10.2026 in den Kategorien Champions League,Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.

It has been revealed that como beat Manchester United 4-1 — and in this case the scoreline really is a fair expression of the game. For long stretches the match was one-sided, not in terms of chance volume but in terms of access: Como dictated in every phase where the ball went, who received it, and under what conditions it had to be played on. United never got on terms in any of those phases.

Recent findings suggest that cesc Fàbregas’s side indicated two things that rarely go together. Out of possession, a pressing structure with clear direction, isolation of one side, and man-marking that applied near the ball only for the action in progress while everything around it was already speculating on the second ball. And in possession, a positional game of remarkable technical maturity that ties opponents in, switches play, and works systematically into the space behind them. The 4-1 is therefore less an outlier than evidence of work that has been built up over recent seasons.

This analysis goes through the phases one by one: first Como in possession and United’s response, then the work against the ball from the high press to defending the box, and finally the goals.

Sources indicate that in build-up, Como moved away from their nominal 4-2-3-1 and sat closer to a 4-3-3, with the eights as the real variable: very free in their movement and above all active in the half-spaces. The base structure stayed stable — a flat four plus a six in front of them, sometimes ahead of the line, sometimes slightly behind the forward line.

Industry observers note that close to their own goal, Como consistently involved goalkeeper Butez as an additional central player in the build-up. That created a five-against-four against United’s front line — awkward on paper, more awkward still in execution, because Como didn’t use the overload to play through but to tie opponents in. From there, the same shape kept appearing on both the right and the left: centre-back, full-back, a player from the half-position in the eight space, and a six alongside. A diamond that wasn’t an end in itself but had a purpose: the diagonal route out.

It has been revealed that como’s build-up structure. From a 4-1 (flat four), the half-positions with Paz and Perrone are added. Small triangles and diamonds emerge. The three attackers ahead of them create additional options in behind.

According to recent reports, one detail deserves particular attention. At times the full-backs stood not wide but flat, in a half-position. That sounds like a nuance, but it had a clear function: it vacated the wing and created the space the eights could drop into — Paz and Perrone did so regularly. If you don’t occupy the wing yourself, you force the opponent to guard it anyway.

ManU got no access near the ball and left large diagonal spaces open on the far side.

Industry observers note that for United’s midfielders this was close to unsolvable. Tielemans, Mount and Andrey Santos spent the whole game struggling to establish any responsibility at all, let alone get into duels. When an eight dropped out, they couldn’t follow, and if one of them was tied in by it, a two-against-one opened up on the far wing. Como didn’t create that situation once; they created it serially.

The decisive mechanism lay in receiving and relaying the ball. The player in the deeper position usually worked with two touches: the first took the ball backwards, the second relayed it to the free teammate. At the end of every one of those actions stood a player with the game in front of him — and from that open position he could switch play.

What made it possible were the preparatory movements. Paz and captain Da Cunha first lured their markers in the wrong direction and then worked with the head start they’d bought. That head start isn’t only space, it’s above all time: time to control the ball first and relay it second, rather than having to do both in one touch.

It has been revealed that A scene in the 17th minute is typical. Mason Mount steps out, Mazraoui goes into the duel at the same time — nominally United are in an overload here. Only neither of them really gets to the opponent, because both are too late. Paz can therefore calmly take his touch backwards and switch play directly with the second, dissolving the pressure before it had even formed.

When the build-up ran down the right, it highlighted in a recurring pattern: Paz and Da Cunha took the first touch backwards or inside and then switched with the left foot out of a closed body position. The players they found were systematically in open positions — Milla, the far-side six, or the wing-to-wing connection directly.

In the second half, Como adjusted the shape and more often played with two sixes, to form the diamonds faster and switch to the far-side six faster. Couto stood out in this: the right-back repeatedly played the chip into the six or ten space — six or seven times in a row during one spell. It was mainly Paz who received the ball there and could launch the attack.

In the second half Como focus on those diagonal spaces and look for them mainly with chipped balls.

Especially striking inside the diamond are the rotations between the players. Because of the connections between them, they moved in rotation depending on running path, space and ball movement. The same recurring spaces were re-occupied. Under pressure on the ball carrier, the outer players pushed flat or ran in behind the opponents; the highest player in the diamond burst out of the cover shadow and became the reference point in depth. On a deep pass, the two wide players released and joined the depth, able to offer themselves again immediately in an open body position. If the pass went via the flat wide players, the spaces in front of the newly introduced ball carrier could be run into. Every rotation, every positional adjustment was coordinated with the others and, in the end, produced a stream of pressure-resolving passes while Manchester United chased the press in vain.

Como bridged the middle third exceptionally quickly, via dribbles at speed and diagonal passes. Behind it stood a recognisable principle: first tie the opponent to one wing, then get behind them via the diagonal, and in the final third do the same thing again. In sum, that produced the shape of a Z — build-up on the right, transition on the left, finish from the right again.

It has been revealed that in this example Como pin ManU in the press with their short passing. Thanks to the extra attacker on the ball-near side they can play through the pressure and switch.

The connections between wingers and striker carried these attacks and were deliberately kept flexible. The wide players sometimes stayed wide, sometimes came short, sometimes tucked inside. Douvikas accordingly either waited deep in front of the line for the chipped ball or, when space opened up on the wing, received the deeper pass and then ran in behind along the wing as soon as the ball sat on the full-back’s open foot. That flexibility produced the overloads on one side, and the overloads produced the central overload.

Recent findings suggest that in the final third one element was added that is rare in fast transition teams: patience. Como drew opponents towards them with dribbles and short passes, used back-passes when needed, and then switched in front of the block. Da Cunha, Baturina and Paz were the three who could tie opponents in and then find the diagonal. They created the positions on the diagonal, were available to receive, and used their space to apply pressure. The block was usually tied in with short touches, the switch and the position behind the opponent prepared, and quick finishes sought.

Sources indicate that the intensity in possession shouldn’t be underestimated. Practically every attack involved at least three or four players, the width was occupied, the centre likewise, and there were multiple options throughout. What they looked for almost every time was the space behind the opponent on the far side — exactly the zone that is closed last when a block shifts across.

Paz brought the right profile for this pattern. A strong left foot cutting inside from the right, he repeatedly dropped into the right-hand blind side of his opponents, got shots away there with few touches, and racked up the most shots of the match. That the finishes generally came off few touches isn’t a detail but the consequence of the time won further back.

As the move continues, Como again look for the blind side of the defenders. Here Douvikas and Paz are positioned in behind, with Da Cunha joining in front of the back line. After briefly pinning the opponents, the switch reaches Da Cunha, who misses the target from distance.

Sources indicate that what carries all of this is the technical execution. Soft passes, sharp ones when the moment called for it, consistently well timed and played into the right foot — for ninety minutes. Passing that secure at that tempo is what makes a variable concept actually retrievable.

According to recent reports, united’s basic problem out of possession was the hybrid. They pressed half man-oriented, but with a plus-one in the last line — a construction that forces compromises in both directions. It demands access up front that it doesn’t fund at the back.

It has been revealed that there were certainly moments when it worked. When Dalot pushed through into the press on the right and passed his man backwards, a clean man-orientation emerged all the way up to the front — and with it a clear assignment for Mount, out of which the ball could be won. But that stayed the exception. Most of the time Dalot sat too flat out of possession, so United couldn’t trigger the duels up front and went into the press a man short.

It has been revealed that mount was the most conspicuous case in this respect. He barely got into a duel across the whole match because the decision to step out always came too late. Against a team that works with preparatory movements, a late decision is practically the same as none: the opponent already has the head start before the journey even begins.

On top of that came a problem on the far side. There, United’s winger frequently failed to protect the depth — usually Mbeumo, who jogged back rather than closing the space. But that was precisely the target zone of Como’s diagonal switches. It allowed them to change sides almost at will and regularly find an open structure on the other side.

The second half brought no improvement. The distances to opponents stayed large, and centrally what was actually intended still didn’t materialise. Michael Carrick’s double change at half-time was meant to bring more physicality to the six with Carlos Baleba, but it didn’t solve the problem — the assignments still didn’t work, the duels in the centre still didn’t happen, and the wide positions dragged the eights out further, which opened new spaces.

It has been revealed that in the end the energy simply wasn’t there to press with the necessary intensity. United’s press became increasingly static, and a static press against an opponent with this passing quality yields not a single ball win — it only hands them the starting positions they’re looking for anyway.

Sources indicate that como started the game in a high press and sustained it above all in the first half, with isolated spells after the break too. It was triggered on back-passes and goal kicks — and, remarkably, by their own goals: after every strike the team immediately pushed high again instead of managing the lead in a deeper block.

Recent findings suggest that the steering ran consistently towards United’s left build-up side. The reason is personnel: Harry Maguire played there with his weaker left foot as the outside foot, and next to him stood another right-footer in Noussair Mazraoui on the left. Two right-footers on one build-up side means the ball always has to be taken back inside to play on — exactly where Como were closing the door. The press was usually triggered by the left-sided forward, with the ball ending up at either Maguire or Mazraoui.

Pressing structure after the change in the second half.

According to recent reports, in the centre Como defended man-oriented, with both sixes pushing very high and taking flat passes into United’s midfielders out of the game. That removed the short route through the middle as an option and left the long ball. But the long ball triggered nothing for United: the second balls went to Como practically every time.

That isn’t chance, it’s running work. The sixes consistently tracked the negative pressing paths back, anticipated the long ball early, and were in front of the line before it arrived. Luis Milla covered the most ground of any player on the pitch in this pattern — recovery runs after being played past, doubling up on the ball, attacking the second ball. When the long ball came from Maguire or one of the full-backs, a six was regularly in front of the line with an intense sprint, sealing the centre, taking away the diagonal follow-up passes and attacking the loose balls.

Defending the long ball and extra support on the second ball.

In a recent development, once the ball was on one side, that side was isolated. The near-side forward had access to the centre-back and dropped back a touch when the pass went to the full-back, so that he covered centre-back and six simultaneously and closed the square pass. The far-side forward marked the goalkeeper. That served two functions at once: it took away United’s escape route via the keeper along with the switch, and it kept a player in position for the moment of the turnover.

It has been revealed that the double pivot worked in a deliberate half-position. The near-side six stayed tight to his man, the far-side one dropped slightly behind him — securing the space and at the same time establishing access to the far-side centre-back in United’s back three.

The last line defended largely man-for-man in the high press, and very tightly. But the decisive detail is the one that carries the whole concept: the man-marking near the ball applied only to the action in progress. Around it, players were already releasing from their assignments and orienting towards the second ball. That is only retrievable at very high intensity — and it’s the reason United’s forced long balls produced not a single usable moment.

When Como dropped a line, the man-orientation at the second height stayed exceptionally high. Here too the back-pass served as the trigger to push up as a unit and tip back into man-marking. If United were in a closed body position, the Comaschi had already pushed up far enough to attack the back-pass at the moment it was played — a pattern that led directly to the 3-0. The half-position was at work there again: closing down level with the centre-back while simultaneously prepared to push through onto the next player deeper.

In a recent development, in the first half Como still had problems assigning the half-positions against ManU’s 3-2-5. In this example Fernandes moves to the wing, Como fail to establish responsibility and access and are played through at mid-height.

Up to half-time, though, Como had a structural problem with this. The pure man-marking didn’t come off cleanly, because of the two sixes in front of the line, one should really have tucked in and taken over the half-position for the centre-backs. That didn’t happen consistently. The consequence: a centre-back stepped out, the space behind him stayed unoccupied, and that was exactly what United kept attacking.

Sources indicate that the pattern of pressing onto Manchester United’s left side continued in the second half, now with Dalot at full-back. The press was still triggered by Douvikas, with the ball-near winger pushing up as a second striker to press the centre-back. Paz focused on the visitors’ ball-near six and Couto pushed through onto Dalot. Through the central connections the game was isolated on one side.

Industry observers note that at half-time Como adjusted. One six moved directly into the line, with the far-side winger pushing in onto the six — they now pressed out of a 5-2-1-2. Lucas Da Cunha pressed through from the right onto Maguire, while Nico Paz picked up United’s six. The central forward pressed the central centre-back and from there carried on to the goalkeeper. The far-side wide midfielder and the remaining six were poised — one onto United’s free six, one onto the far-side centre-back — again in that half-position between opponent and the space to be protected.

ManU building up high against the man-oriented Italians.

According to recent reports, the effect was immediately visible. Como controlled the half-positions, got access right into the last line throughout, and set the rhythm of the match from then on. The adjustment solved exactly the problem the first half had left open, without changing the underlying principle.

Recent findings suggest that in the final phase Como defended from a very deep line inside the box. That left barely any space behind the line to play into — which United hardly looked for anyway. The visitors attacked little depth and rarely occupied the width in the final third, so Como could stay compact without being punished for it.

Recent findings suggest that accordingly, a lot of players stood very centrally in and in front of the box. That produced numerous cover shadows and a numerical superiority around the ball, which allowed them to steer actively within the block rather than merely react. At times they deliberately steered inside, to guide the opponent into the prepared congestion and cover from a deeper position.

Deep back line in the box, centre closed and play steered inside. The box defending allowed the English side shots from distance.

The crucial point is that Como left the gaps open not despite this set-up but because of it. If you pack the box and secure the depth, you give up the space in front of the line — and that is exactly where United were supposed to shoot from.

Recent findings suggest that the numbers vindicate the decision. Taking the conceded goal out of the box, Como allowed nine shots from outside the penalty area across ninety minutes, worth roughly 0.24 xG combined; only three of them were even on target. On top of that, of the four shots inside the box, two came from at least 14 to 15 metres and effectively belong in the long-range category as well. United accepted the invitation, and the shooting quality was perfectly decent — it’s just that with that scoring probability over a whole match, the most likely outcome is precisely what happened.

Tracking the ball for the first goal.

Industry observers note that 1-0, Nico Paz (2′) — The goal comes before United are even set. Como take the goal kick rapidly and play straight to the full-back, luring the visitors into the press — only not cleanly. Mason Mount triggers the pressure and is played past, and on the second ball he goes into the duel as well instead of holding the middle and looking for the space where he could pick the ball up. That is exactly what opens the centre, the space for the second ball is there, and Paz can play it through.

It has been revealed that what follows is the transition principle in its purest form: a quick switch to the diagonal side, then short passes against a very deep line. Matheus Cunha doesn’t pick up the player behind him and leaves the ten space open, where Paz is standing. He needs two touches because neither Cunha from above nor Maguire from his distance gets into the duel. Lammens, for his part, doesn’t defend the goal with his cover shadow but takes the near post — which leaves the far corner to a strong left foot. The curled finish into it is quality, though.

Sources indicate that 2-0, Anastasios Douvikas (49′, assist Paz) — Same zone, same cause. Bryan Mbeumo doesn’t choose to shut the centre but closes the centre-back, which creates the space for Da Cunha, who drives forward and plays Martin Baturina in. Centrally, Mount again fails to pick up his man. Out wide, Amad Diallo, introduced at half-time, generates no pressure centrally, so Mazraoui can’t take over the deep wide player in the first place.

The result is Paz behind the opponent, in the ten space, dribbling unopposed at goal. Matthijs de Ligt establishes no reference to Douvikas’s run in behind and slips as well — a one-against-one with the goalkeeper that Douvikas finishes coolly.

It has been revealed that 3-0, Nico Paz (57′) — The only goal that comes directly out of the work against the ball. Como are in the midfield press in a closed position with access to the inside lane, win the ball there and punish a lapse of concentration in the visitors’ build-up. At the end, Paz is alone in front of Lammens again.

4-0, Jacobo Ramón (76′, assist Kaiki) — This goal comes from a longer possession spell and indicates the assignment problem in its clearest form. Mazraoui is too narrow and has no access to the wide player. Diallo stands in the space with access to neither the central player nor the full-back nor the winger — an orientation that doesn’t work in any direction.

According to recent reports, como switch to Máximo Perrone, who can slide the ball out wide because the space is simply free. From there comes the cross from an open body position, and in the centre Como run a two-against-one at the end of which Ramón scores.

4-1, Joshua Zirkzee (90′) — Como’s only lapse, and one in a phase in which the team had already dropped very deep. United get the ball to the wing, it’s two against two in the box, and the cross is initially only feinted. Zirkzee orients himself well forwards at that moment, while Como’s defenders are already stepping out after the feinted cross. Diallo’s ball in behind the line is strong, the offside call is razor-thin in his favour, and Zirkzee takes two touches before finishing one-against-one with the goalkeeper. A blemish, not a structural problem.

In a recent development, the common denominator — Three of Como’s four goals come in the same zone: the space in front of and behind United’s line that nobody takes responsibility for. Mount is involved in two of those scenes through an assignment he never establishes, Diallo in two more after coming on. Nico Paz is at the heart of three of the four goals, twice as scorer, once as the provider — always out of the opponent’s blind side.

Recent findings suggest that como’s 4-1 has one common cause across every phase, and it lies less in any single idea than in its execution under continuous load. Out of possession they steered, isolated and speculated on the second ball — with man-marking that applied near the ball only for the action in progress and was already dissolved around it. In possession they tied opponents in, switched play and worked systematically into the space behind. Both require eleven players to anticipate a teammate’s decision, and both functioned over the full distance.

The connecting detail is the half-position. In the press, the far-side six stood between opponent and the space to be protected; in possession, the eights worked out of the same zone, and the full-backs occupied it flat in order to vacate the wing for exactly those players. Como, in other words, occupied the position in both directions from which two jobs can be done at once — which is why the side could neither be played past in the press nor be pinned in the build-up.

Recent findings suggest that for United the diagnosis is more uncomfortable than the result. The problem wasn’t individual errors but that the team never, in any phase, got into the duels it needed. The mixture of half man-orientation and a plus-one in the last line funded no access up front, and without access every decision is made too late — from Mount in the centre to Mbeumo failing to secure the far-side depth. Carrick’s double change at half-time was meant to bring physicality to the six with Carlos Baleba, but it changed nothing about the assignments, and in Diallo a player came on wide who reached neither one opponent nor the other in his space. That the energy ran out in the end was a consequence rather than a cause.

That leaves the context. A 4-1 against Manchester United is no proof in itself, and Como’s finishing was exceptionally efficient on the night. What demonstrated regardless of the result, though, is a team with a recognisable, rehearsed answer in all four phases of the game — and one that put a technical maturity on the pitch in possession that you wouldn’t readily credit to a side promoted two years ago.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Les sites FLASHSCORE et SOFASCORE ont figé leurs statistiques à l'issue de la rencontre remportée par les Verts à Reims (1-0), pour le compte de la 13me journée de Ligue 2.
  • Sur les vingt données extraites des deux plateformes sportives, les deux équipes ne sont pas parvenues à se départager : dix statistiques sont en faveur des Verts, les dix autres, fatalement, pour le Stade de Reims.
  • Dans le jeu avec et sans ballon, les Stéphanois ont perdu le match de la possession (46% vs 54%), tout comme ils l'avaient perdu contre Montpellier (45% vs 55%), à Metz (46% vs 54%), au Red Star (41% vs 59%) et à Sochaux (47% vs 53%).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Les sites FLASHSCORE et SOFASCORE ont figé leurs statistiques à l'issue de la rencontre remportée par les Verts à Reims (1-0), pour le compte de la 13me journée de Ligue 2.

Sur les vingt données extraites des deux plateformes sportives, les deux équipes ne sont pas parvenues à se départager : dix statistiques sont en faveur des Verts, les dix autres, fatalement, pour le Stade de Reims. Match nul donc.

Dans le jeu avec et sans ballon, les Stéphanois ont perdu le match de la possession (46% vs 54%), tout comme ils l'avaient perdu contre Montpellier (45% vs 55%), à Metz (46% vs 54%), au Red Star (41% vs 59%) et à Sochaux (47% vs 53%). Cinq défaites en ce qui concerne le monopole du ballon mais quatre victoires et un nul au coup de sifflet final (quatre prétendants à la montée rencontrés). Cependant, les Verts ont devancé leur adversaire du soir dans les duels relatifs à la distance kilométrique parcourue (104,3 km vs 98,3 km) et aux sprints à haute intensité (121 vs 115).

Sources indicate that pour ce qui est des passes, les Champenois sont devant partout : les passes réussies (87% vs 83%), les passes longues réussies (52% vs 33%) ainsi que les passes réussies dans le dernier tiers (74% vs 64%). Après Sochaux, Montpellier, Metz et le Red Star, c'est donc la cinquième fois de la saison que les Stéphanois ne dominent pas leur sujet dans ce domaine, en étant même en dessous de leur moyenne constatée avant cette 13ème journée. Cinq défaites dans le match des passes cette fois-ci, pour quatre victoires et un nul à la fin du temps réglementaire.

Sur le plan offensif, Sainté domine Reims sur cinq des huit métriques remontées avec notamment un xG de 1,45 (vs 0,97), un xGOT de 1,06 (vs 0.16), 21 ballons touchés dans la surface adverse contre 20, 2 occasions à 1 et un pourcentage de précision dans les tirs deux fois plus élevé (43% vs 21%).

Dans le secteur défensif, en revanche, les Verts ont perdu la bataille des duels (46% des duels joués, 44 sur 95) et des tacles réussis (64% vs 75%).

Par ailleurs, les Verts se sont vu attribuer par FLASHSCORE la note globale de 6.9 vs 6.6 pour Reims. Au niveau individuel, c'est Z.Davitashvili qui est élu "homme du match" avec une note de 7.9 (pour 32 minutes de temps passé sur le terrain de jeu) devant A.Boakye (7.6), D.Guindo, le latéral rémois (7.4), I.Cardona (7.3), M.Ndiaye (7.2) à égalité avec deux autres Champenois, S.Kotto et T.Leoni. Enfin, trois autres Stéphanois ont obtenu la note de 7.0 : A.Csongvai, K.Pedro et J.Le Cardinal.

I.Cathro a notamment déclaré : "C'est une victoire très importante. On a été intelligents. L'équipe a appris au fil du match, a été équilibrée. On savait que cet adversaire avait de la qualité et qu'on devait lui donner peu d'opportunités pour s'exprimer". Une victoire très importante effectivement qui permet à Sainté de creuser momentanément un écart conséquent sur Reims : +10 points au soir du 13ème acte de cette Ligue 2.

Dutch progress in Nations League despite 5-0 drubbing in Germany

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (373 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dutchnews

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.
  • The Netherlands came crashing down to earth after hammering Greece as they were outclassed and outmuscled by Germany in Berlin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

The Netherlands came crashing down to earth after hammering Greece as they were outclassed and outmuscled by Germany in Berlin.

Oranje went into the final match of the Nations League group stage with high hopes of recording their first win over their old rivals in seven matches stretching back to 2019.

Instead they suffered their second worst defeat ever at the hands of Germany, but still progressed to the knockout stages thanks to their thumping 7-0 win in Amsterdam on Friday.

Coach Xavi Hernandez was forced to make one change in midfield as Jurriën Timber replaced Barcelona’s Frenkie de Jong, who pulled out with an obturator muscle strain.

Germany shaded the first half and went ahead five minutes before the break when Freiburg striker Derry Scherhant cut in from the left hand side and beat Bart Verbruggen with a curling strike into the top corner.

Scherhant had struck the post minutes earlier, while the Dutch might have taken the lead earlier when Crysencio Summerville slipped in the penalty area as he tried to control a cross by Cody Gakpo.

But in the second half the Dutch fell apart. In the 60th minute Florian Wirtz shoved Denzel Dumfries off the ball and had space to tee up a left-footed shot from the edge of the area that gave Verbruggen no chance.

Nico Schlotterbeck added a third from a free-kick five minutes later, before Wirtz drifted past Gakpo on the right side of the penalty area to score his second.

The humiliation was complete when Brajan Gruda capped a fine attacking performance by firing in a rebound.

Dumfries made no excuses afterwards for what he admitted was a “terrible performance”. “We gave the ball away too easily, left too much space and were too weak in the challenges,” he told NOS. “We can’t let that happen.”.

#222220. Why Liverpool have a point to prove against Man United: Andoni Iraola's side must end rotten run against 'Significant Six' rivals - and Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have to finally step up when it matters

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1372 w)

Why Liverpool have a point to prove against Man United: Andoni Iraola's side must end rotten run against 'Significant Six' rivals - and Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have to finally step up when it matters

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1372 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.
  • Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 23 November 2026.

Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.

Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.

One problem for Andoni Iraola is his side's frailties in the bigger games, which comes into focus this weekend with United in town – despite the desire to make an easy joke about how this is a clash against relegation fodder.

Since thrashing United 7-0 in 2023, Liverpool have beaten their friends in Manchester just once in seven meetings, including two draws and a defeat at Anfield.

Recent findings suggest that to use a cliche, form seems to go out of the window for this fixture. In the last two Anfield meetings, Liverpool have been first and second in the table, United 14th and then tenth. This weekend, it is fourth against 18th, though Pochettino’s side could be bottom by kick-off.

Sources indicate that liverpool’s struggles in bigger games stretch further. Against the so-called 'Big Six’, the Reds have won just two of 12 games since winning the Premier League title. In a ‘mini league’ of those six sides, Liverpool are bottom in the aforementioned period.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side must prove on Sunday they can deliver in the biggest matches.

Manchester United did the double over Liverpool in the Premier League last season.

United did the double over Liverpool last season, Manchester City have beaten them four times in little over 12 months, Arsenal won on Merseyside a month ago.

Sources indicate that so why has this team gone from looking formidable 18 months ago to rather flappable whenever the historic significant boys are in town? Casual neutrals who only tune in for the showpiece Sunday 4.30pm may joke that they have not seen Liverpool play well for a good year.

A lot of the answer to that question comes back to Arne Slot and the issues we documented every week last season, when his side were dull and boring to watch, naked in defence and would capitulate in an instant.

Maybe players like Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola thrive more in intricate spaces rather than the gaping gaps left behind by the attack-minded bigger teams.

Another reason could be the simple fact that these sides are more likely to expose Liverpool’s vulnerabilities, such as the lack of a true defensive midfielder, the poor full backs or the frailties at defending set-pieces.

It has been revealed that anfield has lost its fear factor somewhat, too. Liverpool are top of the Premier League away table with 13 points from 15, but 18th in the home table with just one win in five games.

It has been revealed that city had not won in front of a crowd there since 2003, now they have done it two seasons running. Arsenal had not triumphed at the stadium for 14 years until last month.

Iraola is aware of all this and remarked on Friday: ‘United finished third in the table last season. You are looking at a squad with exactly the same players. They had very, very good results, especially in the second half of the season.

Liverpool bemoaned Ryan Gravenberch’s red card in their home defeat to Manchester City.

The Reds spurned a number of chances when they were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal last month.

‘Now we have just started, this is just 10 games. So, for sure, they will be a lot higher in the table (soon). We have to rate them like this and the truth is the reference we have is that they finished third.

‘We have to look at ourselves because we need the points. We need to improve our home form. It is also a big game in terms of relevance. It’s Liverpool v Manchester United, so we want to play well and we want to win.’.

Asked if he understands the importance of the fixture to fans, Iraola – who spent the weekend off taking in grassroots football and netball games following his kids – mentioned: ‘I am very aware! This is the biggest one in English football. In this country, this is the one.’.

Industry observers note that in Iraola’s first two bigger games, a theme threatened to emerge. Against Manchester City, Liverpool were well in the contest until Ryan Gravenberch’s red card but were toothless when it came to putting their chances away, lacking bite in attack.

The game was there to be won at 0-0, with the Anfield crowd roaring, but the Reds did not have the killer instinct to do so.

Sources indicate that against Arsenal, there were plenty of chances to equalise after the Gunners’ early goal but, again, goalkeeper David Raya could have put his feet up and had a cigar. A lot of territory but nothing to make the defence seriously sweat.

Recent findings suggest that in both cases, Liverpool were on the receiving end of refereeing howlers. Gravenberch’s red was not a red – the first yellow should never be a booking – and Alexander Isak had a stonewall penalty turned down. ProRef has admitted errors.

To take a cynical view, though: in the title-winning campaign, we were rarely sat talking about referees or moaning about narrow misses or unfair results. Liverpool found ways to win and had no excuses.

Liverpool need Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak to step up against the league's big boys.

In a recent development, and that brings us nicely on to Sunday. It feels like the script has been written for weeks.

Indeed, after United lost 3-0 to Bournemouth and the score was read out to huge cheers at Anfield, Daily Mail Sport wrote: ‘Everyone is looking forward to United sacking Michael Carrick and then rocking up at Anfield to win 1-0 with their new manager in a few weeks.’.

It always seems to happen and it feels like United get results against rivals Liverpool and City even when they have felt close to their lowest ebb.

It has been revealed that but Liverpool and Iraola must not allow that to happen. There can be no excuses of ‘latest manager bounce’, refereeing calls or fine margins come Sunday tea time.

Isak and Wirtz simply must step up. It feels harsh that the pair, Wirtz especially, are always in the spotlight but the £125million and £116million signings have flattered to deceive against the massive boys.

Both have been spectacular at times this term but need to show up when it really matters, while £123million addition Barcola is still waiting for his first Premier League goal.

In a recent development, iraola has history with United. As a player, his Athletic Club side beat Sir Alex Ferguson’s great side 5-3 over two legs in Europe.

According to recent reports, ‘I stated at the time, it was one of the best wins of my career,’ he said. 'United, I remember, were champions of the Premier League, got to the Champions League final and lost to Barcelona the year before. We honestly played much better than them.’.

Iraola has remained unbeaten against United into his managerial career, winning two and drawing four of his six meetings with them.

Overall, the former Bournemouth boss has played 38 games against ‘Big Six’ teams in the league: winning ten, drawing ten, losing 18.

According to recent reports, but a win is all that matters on Sunday and it is a chance for Liverpool to set the tempo ahead of a busy festive schedule. After already taking on the current top three, Iraola now contests two rivalries with a trip across the city to Everton next week.

Six of nine pre-Christmas games are at Anfield so there is a real chance to build a head of steam in the league, qualify for the next stage of Europe and get to the Carabao Cup semi-final.

Iraola would welcome those festive gifts but, for Liverpool fans, nothing will be sweeter than giving their old foes a good old walloping on Sunday.

Ayant marqué 3 buts cette saison en championnat des U17 nationaux (contre Villefranche-sur-Saône, Ajaccio et Saint-Priest), l'attaquant stéphanois Izaya Kimpioka fait partie des 34 joueurs sélectionnés en équipe de France U16 pour un stage de 5 jours à Clairefontaine lors duquel il affrontera les U17 du Paris FC (le mercredi 2 décembre à 15h00) et les U17 du VAFC (le jeudi 3 décembre à 11h00).

Industry observers note that il ya quelques mois, du 28 au 31 mai 2026, Izaya Kimpioka avait déjà été convoqué, tout comme Adam Charreyre, à un stage à Clairefontaine, en compagnie des 72 meilleurs jeunes de la génération 2011.Izaya Kimpioka a débuté le football à Sainte-Geneviève en U6 avant de rejoindre Brétigny en U7. Il est ensuite passé au FC Fleury en U11 et a intègré l’INF Clairefontaine durant les années U14 et U15. Il a rejoint l'ASSE cet été, repéré par le duo de scouts stéphanois dans le bassin francilien, Mahamadou Gory et Hamdane Karouni. A l'ASSE, il n'est même pas passé par la case U16 et a intégré immédiatement les U17 de David Le Moal, comptant 8 titularisations, 3 entrées en jeu.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il centrocampista piace a Palladino, che lo ha già allenato alla Fiorentina; Bondo è l’alternativa per gennaio.

It has been revealed that danilo Cataldi è il primo nome nella lista del Bologna per rinforzare il centrocampo a gennaio. Secondo quanto riportato da Corriere dello Sport, L’ipotesi dipende però da due condizioni: che il giocatore abbia superato del tutto il problema fisico con cui ha convissuto negli ultimi mesi e che le richieste di Claudio Lotito per il suo cartellino non siano troppo alte. Il contratto del centrocampista con la Lazio scade a giugno. Se la pista non dovesse concretizzarsi, l’alternativa indicata è Warren Bondo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Sources indicate that il Bologna considera Cataldi una soluzione gradita e fattibile. Il club punta ad acquistare un mediano alla riapertura del mercato di gennaio, una necessità nota già da agosto.

L’interesse del Bologna per Cataldi non nasce ora. Gli uomini dell’area tecnica avevano già pensato di portarlo a Casteldebole nell’anno in cui il centrocampista della Lazio passò invece alla Fiorentina. In viola trovò come allenatore Raffaele Palladino e disputò una grande stagione.

Industry observers note that tra il tecnico e Cataldi c’è stima reciproca. Palladino sarebbe felice di allenarlo di nuovo e anche il centrocampista ha grande considerazione di lui. Giovanni Sartori e Marco Di Vaio, per il momento, non vogliono affrontare pubblicamente il tema del mercato. La fonte ritiene possibile che si siano già mossi per capire prima le intenzioni del giocatore e poi quelle della Lazio.

Per il Bologna, dunque, Cataldi resta la prima scelta, a condizione che il guaio fisico sia completamente alle spalle e che l’eventuale trattativa con Lotito sia sostenibile. Il centrocampista ha 32 anni e arriverà a scadenza contrattuale a giugno.

Se non dovessero esserci le condizioni per arrivare a Cataldi, il Bologna guarda a Warren Bondo. Il centrocampista è attualmente fuori rosa al Milan, dopo aver trascorso il campionato passato nella Cremonese. Anche lui ha già lavorato con Palladino, ai tempi del Monza.

Rispetto a Cataldi, Bondo è un classe 2003 e non occuperebbe un posto in lista. I due profili hanno inoltre un elemento in comune: conoscono il campionato italiano. Palladino e il Bologna cercano rinforzi che non debbano impiegare tempo per adattarsi alla realtà del calcio italiano.

Per quanto possibile, lo stesso criterio guiderà la ricerca di giocatori destinati agli altri reparti. Il discorso è più complicato soprattutto per gli attaccanti: in Italia, chi dispone di profili affidabili tende a trattenerli oppure chiede cifre che il Bologna non è disposto a spendere.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

La réserve a écrasé ce mercredi 4-0 la faible équipe de Hope Team, sélection de joueurs chinois évoluant sous le maillot de l'AJA et dans le groupe A du Challenge Espoirs, où elle affiche un 0 pointé avec 0 but marqué et 18 buts encaissés en 3 matches dont 10 inscrits par Monaco, 4 par le VAFC et 4 par le Paris FC.

Ce match amical aura permis à Sylvain Gibert de donner du temps de jeu à des garçons qui en avaient besoin. Y ont pris part des réservistes, des U19, des U17, un U16 (le néo-international Izaya Kimpioka) mais aussi 3 joueurs à l'essai qui se sont montrés décisifs.

According to recent reports, C'est d'ailleurs sur un coup de pied arrêté tiré par l'un d'entre eux que Mamadou Kanté a ouvert le score une minute avant la mi-temps. Sur un ballon en profondeur d'un deuxième joueur à l'essai, Tidiane Vibert, expulsé dimanche dernier avec les U19 sur le terrain du Cavigal, s'est bien racheté en inscrivant le but du break en début de seconde période.

Mamadou Konté a ôté tout espoir à Hope Team d'un nouveau coup de tête imparable sur un corner de Lenny Marliac. Sur un centre de Noham Akil, le U17 Timothé Demassieux a clôturé le score d'une frappe légèrement déviée par un Chinois au ras du poteau.

La compo : R.Fuleki - Cheikh (c), Benkou, Assoumani (Lengi, 70'), joueur à l'essai (Marliac, 60') - Thouilleux (Demassieux, 46'), Akil, joueur à l'essai (Kimpioka, 60'), Vibert (O.Mendy, 75') - Joueur à l'essai (Freychet, 70'), Konte.

Liverpool's win over Man United was a landmark day for Andoni Iraola - he is playing a style of football that Jurgen Klopp would be proud of, writes LEWIS STEELE

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (797 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • A Liverpool manager wearing a toothy grin and black puffer jacket as he lapped up the adulation of Anfield with three fist bumps in front of the Kop… where have we seen that before?
  • Andoni Iraola may not look as natural at the grand gestures or possess the aura of his predecessor Jurgen Klopp just yet – but this still felt like a landmark day for the Basque manager.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 23 November 2026.

A Liverpool manager wearing a toothy grin and black puffer jacket as he lapped up the adulation of Anfield with three fist bumps in front of the Kop… where have we seen that before?

Andoni Iraola may not look as natural at the grand gestures or possess the aura of his predecessor Jurgen Klopp just yet – but this still felt like a landmark day for the Basque manager.

Playing a heavy-metal style of football that Klopp would be proud of, Iraola has impressed in his early months at Liverpool but craved a real scalp against a rival to turbocharge the feeling among the fanbase and give his tenure true lift-off.

This was the finest day of the fledgling upcoming era as Iraola’s relentless Reds were unstoppable and humiliated their biggest rivals – and the boss must be rubbing his hands at his depth of attacking weapons.

Rio Ngumoha, unbelievably still just 18, was the pick of the bunch and United simply could not get near him, while Florian Wirtz put in his best performance in a Reds shirt and Dominik Szoboszlai looked back to his breathtaking best.

Szoboszlai started the rout with a devastating free-kick and swung an imaginary golf club in celebration, then pretended to watch his tee shot fly into the Anfield Road Stand.

Andoni Iraola is playign a style of football that Jurgen Klopp would be proud of at Liverpool.

Sticking on the Hungarian’s theme, the gulf in quality between these two teams felt like that of a professional golfer compared to a rookie who can barely get the ball off the driving range.

Szoboszlai got his driver out to score a thumping strike and continue his role as the Premier League’s best dead-ball specialist – and Liverpool never looked back from there.

All the talk centred around Mauricio Pochettino’s soft side and the embarrassing sequence of events that led to Lenny Yoro’s early red card but let’s take nothing away from Liverpool, who were breathtaking and unstoppable.

In a recent development, the fact the score was only 4-0 flattered United. To be picky and find criticism in feedback of Liverpool, they were wasteful. This could have been five, six, seven, you name it.

Ngumoha was unplayable. The England international was only four when United won the last of their league titles and Sir Alex Ferguson departed, so he will not remember this team being competent. But the teenager knew the significance of his performance in this fixture.

Sources indicate that his assist for Florian Wirtz was eye-catching, his goal to make it 3-0 deserved after a lung-busting run off the ball. Poor Diogo Dalot will have nightmares for days about Ngumoha’s dancing feet as the Liverpool winger skipped past him time and again.

Recent findings suggest that there were times when Ngumoha played the wrong pass which is the most frightening thing for rivals. This kid is far from the finished product. He will only get better and can be one of the best forwards in the game in a year or so.

He is level-headed unlike some other egotistical young stars and he plays with a smile on his face. Why wouldn’t he?

Rio Ngumoha was unplayable against Manchester United at Anfield and will only get better.

It has been revealed that liverpool will pay a maximum of £6.8million for him, based on add-ons after poaching him from Chelsea two years ago. In the week of Grand Theft Auto IV’s release, the heist of Ngumoha feels like the grandest theft of all (though he is only just old enough to play the video game!).

Those around him are all £100million signings but his ceiling is just as high as that of Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola.

It helps that all four clicked in this game. Wirtz has been excellent this season but has not performed in the bigger fixtures. Conversations after losses to Manchester City and Arsenal centred around Wirtz not showing up.

According to recent reports, the German was everywhere here and United were left to chase shadows. It is not an exaggeration to label this his best Liverpool performance, with an easy-on-the-eye goal and some moments of creative genius.

Barcola destroyed United with his pace, Szoboszlai was a constant menace, while Isak did everything right until it came to finishing several attacks.

And that is the thing that will excite the head coach and should leave rival fans quaking in their boots. This team is full of virtuoso match-winners but all of them have plenty of room to improve. If they do that and all fulfil their potential, the sky is the limit for Iraola’s Liverpool.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Ajax moved into a clear second place in the Eredivisie with a routine 3-0 win against ADO Den Haag, as Feyenood slipped to fifth after losing to local rivals Excelsior.

Davy Klaassen took just three minutes to stroke home the opening goal for Ajax and added a second just before half-time.

By then ADO had been reduced to 10 men following the dismissal of Matteo Waem for hauling down Tolu Arakodare.

But there was a blow for Ajax ahead of next weekend’s visit to Feyenoord when Jorthy Mokio, scorer of the second goal, was taken off injured after an accidental collision with Sékou Sylla.

Feyenoord, who started the month top of the Eredivisie, suffered their first home defeat in the derby against Excelsior since 1980 to continue a slump in form that has seen them draw two and lose four of their last six games.

Givairo Read’s blistering shot gave Feyenoord the lead after just two minutes, but Excelsior were ahead by half-time and made it 3-1 when Casper Windell headed in a corner after 58 minutes. Despite an own goal by Jan Plug, on loan from Feyenoord, Excelsior were not to be denied.

PSV remain a point clear of Ajax at the top of the table after they cruised to a 4-1 win at NEC, with Filip Kostic opening the scoring with his first goal for PSV and his first Eredivisie goal since 2014, when he was playing for Groningen.

Utrecht sacked their managed Anthony Correia after just 14 matches after sinking to 15th place in the table with a 3-2 home defeat to Cambuur.

Correia won just four games after leaving Telstar, the club he led to promotion two seasons ago and where he spent his entire 15-year playing career. Youth team coach Mark Otten will take charge of the first team while Utrecht search for a replacement.

Willem II, searching for their first Eredivisie win in 30 matches, took a shock lead away to Twente despite being reduced to 10 men in the first half when Devin Haen was given space in the area to shoot past Joël Drommel.

The home side struggled to turn their superiority into goals, but an equaliser by Ramiz Zerrouki and a late header by Marko Pjaca gave them the points they needed to rise to third place above Feyenoord.

AZ also overtook Feyenoord as they beat Sparta 5-1 with a dominant second-half display, while Fortuna Sittard kept in touch with the leading group with a typically gritty 1-0 win at Go Ahead Eagles.

Go Ahead Eagles 0-1 Fortuna Sittard.

Sparta Rotterdam 1-5 AZ Alkmaar.

Twente Enschede 2-1 Willem II Tilburg.

Sources indicate that L'ancien Vert, Mathys Saban opère désormais au Mâcon 71 (N2), après un passage au Luxembourg (Titus Petange, Racing FC Union). Au sortir d’une crise interne marquée par une grève de l’entraînement, Mâcon 71 jouait un match key sur le terrain de la réserve d'Annecy. À dix contre onze (après l'exclusion de l'ancien Vert, Israël Kinunga) et après avoir été rattrapé sur penalty, les Mâconnais ont montré qu’ils savaient réagir. C'est Mathys Saban, entré en jeu à la 71ème, qui a donné la victoire (1-2) aux siens, à la toute dernière minute du match. Un autre ancien Vert, Yoann Greco est entré en jeu à la 65ème.Avec 11 points, Mäcon 71 pointe à la 7ème place, à 8 points du leader Bourgoin dans le championnat de N2.

Mathys Saban (24 ans), joueur offensif polyvalent, est arrivé au centre de Formation de l'ASSE en 2017, en provenance de l'US Torcy qui a fourni aux Verts Lamine Ghezali, Alexandre Valbon, Josué Gago et Marwan Nzuzi, Lucas Gourna-Douath, Mathis Amougou, Fodé Camara, Axel Dodote. Il a gravi toutes les étapes de la formation et signé son premier contrat pro de 3 ans avec l'ASSE le 5 juin 2020, contrat qui sera prolongé de 2 ans en février 2023.En 2020-2021, il joue son premier match en pro, le 23 mai 2021, 12 minutes lors de ASSE-Dijon : 0-1.En 2021-2022, il participe à 3 matchs de Ligue 1 : - 21 août 2021, 21 minutes : ASSE-LOSC : 1-1- 28 août 2021 : 19 minutes : OM-ASSE : 3-1- 12 septembre 2021 : 30 minutes : Montpellier-ASSE : 2-0En 2022-2023, il participe à 3 matchs de Ligue 2 qui se soldent par 3 défaites, et 1 match en Coupe de France : - le 29 octobre 2022, Coupe de France, 30 minutes : ASSE-Rodez : 0-0 (3-4 tab)- le 7 novembre 2022, 45 minutes, Metz-ASSE : 3-2- le 12 novembre 2022, 17 minutes : ASSE-Rodez : 0-2  - le 26 décembre 2022, 33 minutes : Annecy-ASSE : 2-1.

It has been revealed that le 31 août 2023, il est prêté au club luxembourgeois de l'Union Titus Petange pour la saison 2023-2024. Victime d’une rupture du tendon d’achille au début du printemps 2024 lors de son prêt à l’Union Titus Pétange, Mathys Saban revient à l'ASSE pour la saison 2024-2025 mais ne joue que 77 minutes en N3 pour sa 8ème et dernière saison sous le maillot vert. Il retourne  dans le Grand-Duché durant l'été 2025 (au Racing Football Club Union Lëtzebuerg), et inscrit en septembre 2025 son premier but en L1 luxembourgeoise. Malheureusement son contrat est rompu début 2026 et, après 6 mois sans club, il rejoint donc le Mâcon 71 qui a raté de peu l'accession au Championnat National, devancé par Hauts Lyonnais.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 09:00 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • In what transpired to be a lively Sky TV studio at Anfield, Daniel Sturridge turned in one of his own performances of the season.
  • The former Chelsea and Liverpool striker is proving himself a pundit of real substance and he cut to the heart of one of the more ridiculous notions of the week, namely that a week away with Jurgen Klopp had solved all Florian Wirtz’s problems at a stroke.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By IAN LADYMAN, FOOTBALL EDITOR.

Published: 07:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 09:00 EST, 23 November 2026.

In what transpired to be a lively Sky TV studio at Anfield, Daniel Sturridge turned in one of his own performances of the season.

The former Chelsea and Liverpool striker is proving himself a pundit of real substance and he cut to the heart of one of the more ridiculous notions of the week, namely that a week away with Jurgen Klopp had solved all Florian Wirtz’s problems at a stroke.

‘I think we should give credit to Andoni Iraola,’ he remarked as we all breathed a sigh at the sound of some common sense.

The obsession with Klopp among many people who support and follow Liverpool remains terrifyingly real and the former Anfield manager plays to it.

But to suggest – as many who should know better have done – that Klopp managed to fix Wirtz in four sessions last week is as lazy and ridiculous as it is utterly disrespectful to current Liverpool manager Iraola.

It has been revealed that wirtz had a good couple of games with his national team, for sure. He scored three goals which will have done much for confidence. He was fabulous against Manchester United's ten men.

Florian Wirtz has found his form at just the right time for Liverpool.

Reds boss Andoni Iraola deserves credit for the German's transformation this season.

But anybody who has watched even a small portion of Liverpool’s game this season will have seen a player gradually growing in stature and finally, it seems, adjusting to the largely unique rhythms of the Premier League.

Sources indicate that iraola is a talented coach. Talk to players and staff at Bournemouth and they will tell you that. He improves footballers and steadily he is bringing his influence to bear on Wirtz.

The 23-year-old still has some way to go. He can still look half a yard too slow on occasion. But he has created 29 Liverpool chances from open play this season.

Klopp can’t take any credit for that.

It tends to be the execs rather than the managers who get the blame at United but Mauricio Pochettino sadly had his fingerprints on what happened on Merseyside.

He was right to complain about the sending off of Leny Yoro. Alexander Isak was never getting the ball and referee Sam Barrott should have given himself time to consider that before getting the red card out.

In those situations the defender should be given the benefit of any doubt.

The decision has an enormous impact on the game, something that seemed to pass many people by.

Nevertheless the passage of play had at its inception a horror moment from Matthijs de Ligt that most of us could have seen coming the moment the team sheet dropped.

Sometimes it doesn’t pay for a manager to try and be the smartest bloke in the room.

Mauricio Pochettino should shoulder some of the blame for United's dismal defeat at Anfield.

BERRADA INTERVENTION NOT USEFUL FOR UNITED.

No doubt the decision to plonk Omar Berrada in front of a TV camera was driven by good intentions by United.

The club’s executives had been accused of hiding while Old Trafford burned so here was one of them, sitting smartly in front of a huge club crest, ready to tell the world that everything would be OK.

The only problem is that the words of Berrada, United’s chief executive, have arguably made things worse.

Berrada didn’t catch much of a break over the weekend.

Just 48 hours after telling the world that United were happy with their ‘nine defenders’  Pochettino’s team were given such a chasing at Anfield that one wondered if the upcoming manager may be tempted to chuck all of them on at the same time.

Recent findings suggest that none of this is about luck, however. Neither good nor bad. It’s about planning and the lack thereof.

Liverpool, remember, also had a major defensive problem over the summer.

Omar Berrada's surprise appearance on Sky Sports has made things worse for Man United.

In a recent development, the two full-backs bought in the summer of 2025 – Jeremie Frimpong and Milos Kerkez – had struggled while another – Conor Bradley – was injured. In the centre, Ibrahima Konate had left for Real Madrid while young prospect Giovanni Leoni had not played since suffering a dreadful knee injury on his debut last year.

That left Virgil Van Dijk, Jeremy Jacquet and Joe Gomez. Liverpool could have struggled on. They could have counted numbers and hoped. They could have prayed for better form and fitness from the defenders they had.

But that would have been unfair on incoming manager Iraola. So in mid-August they took the Uruguayan international Ronald Araujo on loan from Barcelona and it has transpired to be a signing utterly fundamental to Liverpool’s season so far.

In a recent development, there was little fuss and fanfare about the deal. All the noise was reserved for the £125million winger Bradley Barcola.

Sources indicate that but Araujo – signed as a centre-half – is a former Barcelona captain and has solved Liverpool’s right-back problem at a stroke. He was as unfussy and effective against United yesterday as he has been all season.

This is how recruitment at substantial clubs works. They identify problems and use their data, imagination and contacts to solve them. They don’t count the number of bodies in the dressing room and then sit on their hands telling themselves it is enough.

Every United supporter in the land could have told Berrada and his friends that United needed defensive quality in the summer. But United thought they knew best and were wrong.

It is genuinely terrifying to think just what they may do next.

The second most productive footballer in terms of assists in the league is Brighton’s Pascal Gross but the German was left as bemused as anyone as his team somehow managed to lose a game they dominated at Hull.

Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler has said he wants his players to behave like a major team but perhaps some naivety let them down as Hull scored two in added time on Humberside.

The first of Ollie McBurnie’s goals came in the 92nd minute on the back of a quick counter and it was one that could have been stopped at source by what Pep Guardiola used to call a ‘technical foul’ – a trip or a nudge – before the ball had even crossed the halfway line.

Nobody wishes to encourage foul play but the truth is that Guardiola’s City would not have conceded that goal. Nor, for that matter, would Arsenal.

Brighton's naivety saw them suffer a surprise defeat by Hull City on Sunday.

At the Etihad, Enzo Maresca gave Phil Foden a start ahead of Rayan Cherki and the City playmaker showed some glimpses of his fabulous talent.

Nevertheless the longer this period of uncertainty goes on for Foden, the harder it is to work out how it ends.

Maresca wants to play with two out and out wide players at City.

Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye started in the draw against Fulham while Antoine Semenyo will play when he is fit.

So with Cherki established as City’s creative hub just behind Haaland, Foden is on the fringes a little.

According to recent reports, he signed a contract in June and is now tied to the club until 2030. Equally, Foden will be 27 next May and should be approaching his physical and creative peak.

Meanwhile Cole Palmer’s frustrations with life at Chelsea – highlighted in this column earlier this season – have now boiled over with a show of petulance at the end of his team’s Stamford Bridge hammering at the hands of Leeds.

The more this unfolds, the more it feels like Palmer is at the wrong club.

It has been revealed that palmer – for all that he tries to suggest otherwise – is an emotionally complex young athlete. He can be unpredictable and dramatic.

He needs calm around him, not persistent drift.

Cole Palmer's petulance at Stamford Bridge on Saturday has left us asking: Is he at the wrong club?

Another stunning result for Daniel Farke’s Leeds who now sit sixth in the table with the second best defensive record in the top flight.

Farke remains out of contract next summer and that still feels odd.

The club’s favourite media outlets told us last month that an ‘agreement had been reached in principle’ but still no white smoke from Elland Road.

LONG ROAD AHEAD FOR THE FRESH KID.

Tottenham have crept into the top half for the first time this season after beating Ipswich with credit due to manager Roberto de Zerbi for handing teenager Luca Williams-Barnett his chance.

With major money summer signings Savio and Omar Marmoush sitting on the bench, Williams-Barnett scored the opening goal and became the fourth youngest player in history to score on his first Premier League start.

Of the three ahead of him in the list, Canadian Daniel Jebbison, now 23, presently sits on the Bournemouth bench, Danny Cadamarteri’s career became rather itinerant once he made the last of his 94 Everton league starts while Mark Cullen travelled from Hull to Bamber Bridge via outposts such as Luton, Blackpool, Port Vale, Hartlepool and Fylde.

Williams-Barnett will have enjoyed his weekend but history tells us the road ahead may not be straight.

Luca Williams-Barnett became the fourth youngest debut goalscorer in Premier League history.

Of the upcoming managers in this season’s top division, it has taken time for some to find their feet.

Iraola now has a statement Anfield win, for example, while at Bournemouth and Fulham Marco Rose and Alvaro Arbeloa no longer have to look at the league table through their fingers.

At Newcastle, it appears rather more complicated.

Eddie Howe’s replacement Matthias Jaissle doesn’t look chuffed with the players he was handed in the summer window but historical issues stalk him too.

Last season’s big money flop Yoane Wissa started this one well and looked ready to fly after starring and scoring in an August win at Spurs.

That was the £50million forward’s last goal, though, and he also only has one assist to his name.

On Saturday in the gutsy draw with Arsenal he came on in the 83rd minute and that spoke volumes.

One player whose career has headed the other way is Aston Villa defender Victor Lindelof.

The Swede was signed on a free from Manchester United largely to make the numbers up in August 2025 but his rise to prominence has been such that Match of the Day were moved to note his absence through injury from the team that drew with Sunderland at Villa Park.

It has been revealed that lindelof is 32 now but has just signed a new contract at Villa. Another one to benefit from Unai Emery’s regenerative elixir.

Unai Emery's coaching magic has helped transform the fortunes of Victor Lindelof.

If this weekend has been – in part – about defenders then the Fulham recruitment staff deserve their props too.

The west London club had conceded seven goals in losing their opening three league games before Austrian defender David Affenbruger arrived on the last day of the summer window.

Debuting in the 0-0 draw at Liverpool that followed, Fulham have since lost just one of the seven subsequent games in which he has played.

Recent findings suggest that the fee? £8.5million. Further proof that it really can be done.

Marathon skater Judith Krabbenborg has taken advantage of the early cold snap to smash the world one-hour record for skating on natural ice.

The 29-year-old took to the ice in Winterswijk, Gelderland, at 8.30am on Tuesday and covered a distance of 34 kilometres 878 metres, beating the previous women’s record by 2.6 kilometres.

“I could feel my legs and my back hurting at the end, but there were so many people standing on the sidelines that it gave me energy,” she told NOS.

In a recent development, the previous record, set four years ago by Femke Mossinkoff, also in Winterswijk, was the first official time for the hour by a woman on natural ice. On the same day Bart Vreugdenhil set the current men’s record of 36 kilometers 717 metres.

Most skating records are set on artificial ice, but Winterswijk is one of three arenas where the local club has been able to create a natural arena for early-morning skaters during the recent cold weather.

The all-time women’s record is 40 kilometres 569 metres, set by another Dutch skater, Carien Kleibeuker, in Inzell, Austria, in 2015.

The rink at Winterswijk closed a few hours after Krabbenborg’s record-breaking skate as the ice started to melt, but it is expected to be available again on Wednesday morning.

Dans Le Patriote du Beaujolais, l'ancien gardien et capitaine caladois Franck Laurent se remémore son 16e de finale de Coupe de France perdu en aux tirs au buts contre les Verts (2-2, 1-3 tab). Extraits.

In a recent development, "Notre coach, Jean-Michel Picollet (photo), était à fond pour les Verts. C'était le derby pour nous. On était tellement contents de tomber sur eux ! Je me souviens encore de la causerie du coach, comme si c'était hier. Son message était clair et net. On allait respecter Saint-Etienne à 200% mais par contre, on allait jouer notre match à fond. Le coach nous disait qu'il y avait un truc à faire. Il nous avait mis dans cette position-là, mentalement on était prêt. On en a profité un maximum. Sur un match, on avait nos chances. On jouait sur notre terrain. Eux n'avaient pas l'habitude de ce genre de pelouse. Il y a des facteurs, dans ce genre de match, qui font que tu transcendes, que tu te mets au niveau de l'événement, tu joues ta chance à fond.

Industry observers note that ce match, on en parlait tous les jours entre nous. Du début à la fin, on a vécu les choses à fond ! Ce match-là, contre Saint-Etienne, ça fait 16 ans qu'il a été joué. On m'en parle régulièrement. Pourtant, je ne suis plus du tout dans le foot. Quand on se croise, entre joueurs de cette époque, les premiers mots portent toujours sur ce match. On est liés à vie avec cette aventure de Coupe de France. C'est un petit bout de l'histoire du FCVB. J'ai eu la chance d'être là, au bon moment. Dans une carrière, ce n'est pas si évident de laisser des traces pareilles dans un club !

Les conseils que je donnerais aux Caladois d'aujourd'hui avant d'aller à Geoffroy Guichard, ce samedi ? Le contexte est totalement différent. C'est une Ligue 2 contre une Ligue 3. Il y a des joueurs professionnels des deux côtés. Je ne sais pas si je peux leur donner un conseil, à mon niveau. Mais même pour eux, ça reste des matches magnifiques à vivre. J'espère qu'ils vont arriver à s'extraire du championnat pour profiter pleinement de ce match, et tout donner. Derrière, ça peut renforcer le groupe.".

Ancien meneur de jeu des U17 de l'ASSE sacrés champions de France en 2013 (avec notamment Léo Pétrot, Dylan Chambost, Jonathan Bamba et Allan Saint-Maximin), le numéro 10 de Saint-Paul-en-Jarez (R3) Alexandre Assaf s'est confié au Progrès avant de défier ce dimanche Chassieu-Décines (R1) en Coupe de France. Extraits.

"Le président m’a proposé quelque chose d’inédit pour moi en me disant “je ne te veux pas pour mettre 40 buts par saison mais parce que j’ai beaucoup de bons jeunes qui vont monter et j’aimerais que tu les encadres, que tu les aides à se développer”. J’ai accepté direct. Je sortais de 7 saisons à Monistrol où j'ai connu 2 montées. Redescendre ce n’est pas grave, je donne plus d’importance au projet qu’au niveau.

Je parle beaucoup aux jeunes, j’essaye de les aider à passer le cap, je leur dis d’être patients quand ils jouent moins… Je suis toujours un peu décisif mais surtout content quand eux le sont. Je suis plus passeur que buteur maintenant, je préfère donner que marquer. J’ai un rôle de trentenaire, ça fait mal à dire (rires). Dimanche, en termes d’ambiance, je pense que ça va être un truc que je n’ai jamais vu. Ça va être extraordinaire.".

Chelsea striker Emmanuel Emegha was robbed after leaving Stamford Bridge on Saturday evening, with the 23-year-old Dutchman having scored in his first start for the club.

Despite grabbing the game's first goal while filling in for the injured Joao Pedro, the Blues were beaten 4-1 by Leeds United and booed both at half-time and full-time.

Daily Mail Sport approached Chelsea and the Metropolitan Police on Sunday morning after hearing that the forward's mobile phone had been stolen after he left the stadium the night before.

Neither stood up the information, but Emegha has now confirmed there was an incident, writing in an Instagram post on Sunday night: 'Unfortunately after the game I was robbed. I am okay and thankfully no one was hurt. Thanks for the messages of support.'.

According to recent reports, emegha signed for Chelsea from Strasbourg in the summer on a pre-agreement. The transfer fee between the sister sides has never been disclosed. He has won two caps for the Netherlands national team to date.

Industry observers note that an interview with Emegha was included in Saturday's match-day programme in which he said: 'I'm a winner, I'm a fighter. I would do anything to win. If I need to block a ball with the front of my face, I will do it.

Emmanuel Emegha has revealed he was robbed on Saturday after Chelsea's 4-1 loss by Leeds.

On Sunday, the Chelsea striker revealed the incident had happened to him on Instagram.

He put the Blues ahead at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon - his first goal for the club.

In a recent development, 'I'm quick, I know how to make runs in behind, and I know that I can be a nightmare for all the defenders. Nobody has seen me yet. When my time comes, I will be ready, and I know that the stadium will love my energy.'.

It coincided with him being handed his first start for the Blues and scoring his first goal via a nice left-footed finish. However, Chelsea's 1-0 lead lasted only three minutes as Leeds capitalised on suspect defending to equalise, and then deservedly won.

Noah Okafor scored twice, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brenden Aaronson got one goal each.
